sections.title: Lane Change
sections.description: Automatic lane change timing and behavior

items.title: Auto Lane Change by Blinker
items.description: Set a timer to delay the auto lane change operation when the blinker is used. No nudge on the steering wheel is required to auto lane change if a timer is set. Default is Nudge.
items.details: Please use caution when using this feature. Only use the blinker when traffic and road conditions permit.

items.title: Auto Lane Change: Delay with Blind Spot
items.description: Toggle to enable a delay timer for lane changes when blind spot monitoring (BSM) detects a vehicle in your blind spot.

sections.title: nrdr Learned Params
sections.description: Live-learned vehicle parameters.

items.title: Learn Steer Ratio (Auto)
items.description: When ON (Auto), uses openpilot's live-learned steer ratio. When OFF, uses the car's static base value. Turn OFF if the learned value drifts and hurts performance.

items.title: Learn Tire Stiffness (Auto)
items.description: When ON (Auto), uses the live-learned tire stiffness factor. When OFF, uses the static base value of 1.0.

items.title: Learn Angle Offset (Auto)
items.description: When ON (Auto), uses the live-learned steering angle offset. When OFF, uses a static 0.0 offset. Turn OFF if a bad learned offset is pulling the car to one side.

sections.title: nrdr Lateral Tuning
sections.description: Lateral tuning specific to the nrdr fork.

items.title: Run Tune Report Scan
items.description: Flip ON to scan every drive log into a tune report. The device flips it back OFF on the next start.

items.title: Car & Tune Info
items.details: Your car's loaded profile and lat/long kp/ki/kf, written by the device once it fingerprints the car. Shown on the cluster's Car & Tune Info row and via the device's own settings.

items.title: StarPilot PID Additions
items.description: The borrowed turn-in / unwind / per-direction output scaling (the StarPilot half of _pid_output_scale) not built for Honda. Off = clean banded PID/F + rate-damping D, your center boost kept. Turn on to A/B it against the raw base.

items.title: Low Speed Proportional Scale (Below 25mph)
items.description: Scales the proportional (P) term below 25 mph. Higher = more error correction (tighter, can cut corners); lower = looser with wider swings.

items.title: Low Speed Integral Scale (Below 25mph)
items.description: Scales the integral (I) term below 25 mph. Builds correction over time to erase steady-state error; too high oscillates.

items.title: Low Speed Feedforward Scale (Below 25mph)
items.description: Scales the feedforward (kf) term below 25 mph. Follows the commanded angle rather than error, adding authority without amplifying noise. 100% = tuned value (static).

items.title: Standard Speed Proportional Scale (25-50mph)
items.description: Scales the proportional (P) term between 25 and 50 mph.

items.title: Standard Speed Integral Scale (25-50mph)
items.description: Scales the integral (I) term between 25 and 50 mph.

items.title: Standard Speed Feedforward Scale (25-50mph)
items.description: Scales the feedforward (kf) term between 25 and 50 mph. 100% = tuned value (static).

items.title: Highway Proportional Scale (50mph+)
items.description: Scales the proportional (P) term above 50 mph.

items.title: Highway Integral Scale (50mph+)
items.description: Scales the integral (I) term above 50 mph.

items.title: Highway Feedforward Scale (50mph+)
items.description: Scales the feedforward (kf) term above 50 mph. 100% = tuned value (static).

items.title: Rate Damping (D) Strength
items.description: The derivative term openpilot normally can't use. Adds torque opposing how fast the wheel is moving, which damps the low-speed oscillation plain P can't (the wheel is torque-commanded, so P alone rings). Relies on a clean steering-rate signal and a low-lag EPS - which this car has. 0 = off. Raise until the low-speed wobble flattens; too high makes turn-in feel heavy.

items.title: Rate Damping Fade-Out Speed
items.description: Speed at which rate damping tapers to zero. Damping is strongest at a standstill and gone by this speed, where tire self-aligning torque resumes damping the steering itself. Keeps the D term out of your highway feel.

items.title: Center Boost
items.description: Extra error correction added while driving straight, as a boost on top of the normal output (0.50 = 50% boost). One static value across all speed ranges. Sometimes the perfect lateral tune is too soft for driving in a straight line.

items.title: Center Boost Threshold (deg)
items.description: How centered should the steering wheel be when center boost is actually active?

items.title: Center Boost Minimum Speed
items.description: Below this speed center boost is disabled. Center boost is meant for straight, higher-speed roads; gating it off at low speed stops the wheel from oscillating at stops and in parking-lot crawling.

items.title: 2D Auto-Tuner (Learned Trim)
items.description: Learns a per-(speed, angle) feedforward trim live while you drive, cancelling the systematic over/under-turn the tune report measures. A bounded, slow, gated correction on top of the base PID/F + D - the PID always does the driving. Off by default; Reset below wipes what it has learned.

items.title: Auto-Tuner Strength
items.description: Hard cap on how much steering authority the learned trim may add, as a percent of full output. The learner can never exceed this no matter how long it runs. Start low; raise once you trust it.

items.title: Auto-Tuner Learning Speed
items.description: How fast the trim adapts to the measured error. Lower = slower, calmer, safer; higher = converges quicker but reacts more to each drive. 0 freezes learning (the trim it already has still applies).

items.title: Reset Learned Trim
items.description: Wipes the learned map back to zero on the next drive, then flips itself off. Use it to start the auto-tuner fresh after a base-tune change or a bad learning session.

items.title: Unwind Integrator Freeze
items.description: Freezes the PID integrator while the steering is returning toward center, so it doesn't hold torque through the unwind.

items.title: Unwind Lookahead
items.description: Reads the model's planned path to start unwinding earlier, before the instantaneous desired curvature drops.

items.title: Unwind Boost Duration
items.description: How long the extra unwind feedforward is held at the start of each unwind before it fades out. Caps the low-speed return assist so it doesn't keep pushing torque through a long unwind. 0 = off.

items.title: Unwind Feedforward Multiplier
items.description: Peak feedforward multiplier during an unwind, strongest at a standstill and fading to 1x (no boost) by about 22 mph. Raise for more low-speed return authority if the wheel is lazy coming back to center.

items.title: Increase Driver Override Hysteresis
items.description: Reduces the likelihood of false driver override detections (resulting in dropped torque) on sensitive Honda EPS platforms by doubling the override threshold below.

items.title: Driver Override Threshold
items.description: Raw steering torque sensor reading above which you are considered to be steering (driver override). 1200 is Honda's stock threshold; on the few cars with a different stock threshold, your value is applied proportionally so 1200 always means stock.

items.title: Override Threshold Center Boost
items.description: When the wheel is within the Center Boost degree band (on a straight), this lower override threshold applies instead of the one above - so you can override easily on straights while curves keep the higher threshold and do not drop torque from a false override. Set equal to Driver Override Threshold to disable.

items.title: Pass-through assist torque on override
items.description: When enabled, openpilot resets the EPS internal state which determines whether it is in lane assist mode or not. As such, enabling this will make the final override feel exactly the same as normal driving (after fade is completed), and when disabled the steering rack may carry on a more resistive feeling.

items.title: Override Torque Fade Down
items.description: Controls how quickly steering torque fades out when driver override begins.

items.title: Override Torque Fade Up
items.description: Controls how quickly steering torque fades back in after driver override ends.

items.title: Override Torque Retain
items.description: Controls how much openpilot steering torque remains when the override has gone past Override Torque Fade Down.

items.title: Low Pass Filter (tau)
items.description: Filter that smooths steering response at the cost of adding lag. Tune to the least amount possible before oscillations begin. Live tests show that going above 0.1 tau rapidly increases the possibility of lag-induced oscillations.

items.title: Low Pass Filter Tau (Below 25mph)
items.description: Low-pass filter time constant (seconds) below 25 mph.

items.title: Standard Tau (25-50mph)
items.description: Low-pass filter time constant (seconds) between 25 and 50 mph.

items.title: Highway Tau (50mph+)
items.description: Low-pass filter time constant (seconds) above 50 mph.

items.title: Notch Filter
items.description: Removes a narrow EPS chatter band (around 7Hz) without the lag a low pass filter adds.

items.title: Notch Frequency
items.description: Frequency (Hz) of the band eliminated from the controller. If you know what Hz your EPS growls at, this can help block that out without adding any extra lag into the controller. Best used in pair with a well-tuned low pass filter.

items.title: Notch Q / Width
items.description: Tolerance of the removed frequency. Higher = smaller portion removed, lower = wider (nearby frequencies will be removed as well).

items.title: Legacy Steer Delta Rate Limiter
items.description: Limits how quickly requested steering torque can rise or fall. This is an older system of limiting and may no longer prove useful compared to the low pass and notch filters.

items.title: Steer Delta Up
items.description: Controls the maximum upward steering torque rate when the rate limiter is enabled. Too low will add lag.

items.title: Steer Delta Down
items.description: Controls the maximum downward steering torque rate when the rate limiter is enabled. Too low will add lag.

items.title: Minimum Steer Speed
items.description: Below this speed no steering torque is commanded at all. 0 = steer at any speed (stock). For those who don't want the wheel moving at a standstill or parking-lot speeds.

items.title: Ford: OEM-Style Lateral
items.description: Ford only. Replaces stock curvature-only steering with Ford's full four-signal command (adds curvature-rate plus a lane-centering path-angle), the way the factory system actually drives. Targets the two stock complaints - the wheel fighting you after you grab it, and running out of steering authority in vigorous turns. OFF = stock curvature-only path, unchanged. BETA - first test on an empty road with hands ready. No effect on non-Ford cars.

items.title: Ford: Human Turn Detection
items.description: When you hold the wheel into a turn past 45 degrees, openpilot stops commanding steering so it is not fighting you, then ramps smoothly back in when you let go instead of snapping. This is the fix for the wheel trying to throw you off the road after you touch it. Only active when OEM-Style Lateral is on.

items.title: Ford: Lane Positioning
items.description: Drives the path-angle signal with a lane-centering PID for extra steering authority and tighter in-lane position - the main lever against running out of torque. Engages at highway speed and steps aside during auto lane changes. Only active when OEM-Style Lateral is on.

items.title: Ford: Lane Positioning Strength
items.description: How hard the lane-centering path-angle pulls toward lane center. 100 percent is baseline. Raise for stronger centering, lower if it feels busy. Only used when Lane Positioning is on.

items.title: Ford: Max Lateral Accel
items.description: Raises the lateral-acceleration ceiling that caps how hard the car will corner - the most direct knob for running out of torque. Stock is about 2.4, set low on purpose because the safety model cannot see road banking. Raising it gives more cornering authority but removes that conservative margin; increase in small steps and validate on-road. Only used when OEM-Style Lateral is on.

sections.title: nrdr Special
sections.description: Dashboard, diagnostics, and special features.

items.title: Injection Test (Caution!)
items.description: When enabled, the lateral PID output scale is multiplied by 999%. This is a diagnostic stress test to see how the car reacts to a massive steering command. Use with extreme caution on a safe, empty road.

items.title: Alternative Dashboard Speed Design
items.description: Repurposes the cluster's set-speed slot (requires openpilot longitudinal). Lead Speed shows the lead's speed in whole mph ("Stopped" below 1 mph, "--" with no lead). GPS Speed shows the comma's own true speed. Cluster Speed shows exactly what the dash cluster reads.

items.title: Alternative Dashboard Distance Design
items.description: Repurposes the cluster's distance bars / mini car (requires openpilot longitudinal). Radar closes the bars in as the lead approaches. Velocity pushes the bars out under acceleration and pulls them in under braking. Non-stock designs stay on the cluster permanently, even when not engaged.

items.title: Clear Dashboard Fault Codes
items.description: Forces the cluster's FCM/icon fault bits off and suppresses the stock FCW chime. Lets a car with a dead or absent stock camera run a clean dash. Turn OFF for stock openpilot behavior (camera values passed through, FCW chime active).

items.title: Spoof Camera Messages
items.description: Dead camera only - keeps the camera's CAMERA_MESSAGES broadcast alive so the cluster never raises "Auto High Beam System Problem" (that fault is a message timeout, not a code). Leave OFF if your stock camera works.

items.title: Cruise Button Sub-Mode
items.description: Dynamic HUD - pressing the distance button or set/resume first wakes a preview on the cluster (current personality on the bars, set speed if engaged, all blinking). Only presses made during the preview actually change the personality or set speed. The blink starts lazy and accelerates continuously until it cuts off.

items.title: Sub-Mode Visibility Time
items.description: How long the preview stays on the cluster after a button press. The blink ramp always spans the whole window, slow at the start and rapid right before it falls off.

panels.label: Cruise
panels.description: Longitudinal control, speed limits, and cruise behavior

items.title: Dynamic Experimental Control
items.description: Let the model decide when to use sunnypilot ACC or sunnypilot End to End Longitudinal.

items.title: Disengage Cruise on Accelerator Pedal
items.description: When enabled, pressing the accelerator pedal will disengage longitudinal control.

items.title: Driving Personality
items.description: Standard is recommended. In aggressive mode, sunnypilot will follow lead cars closer and be more aggressive with the gas and brake. In relaxed mode sunnypilot will stay further away from lead cars. In econ mode sunnypilot keeps the longest following distance for smooth, efficient driving. On supported cars, you can cycle through these personalities with your steering wheel distance button.

sections.title: nrdr Longitudinal Tuning
sections.description: Longitudinal tuning specific to the nrdr fork.

items.title: Longitudinal PID Tune Scale
items.description: Scales longitudinal PID controller values from their configured base tune.

items.title: Cruise Mismatch Correction
items.description: Correct slight variances in final cruising target speed to better match the current and set speeds together. Tire, suspension, and other vehicle dynamics can affect this including manufacturer design. If your car permanently drives at 71mph set at 70mph, lower this until correct on a flat road, or vice versa for the opposite problem.

items.title: Keep Feedforward Static
items.description: When ON, the longitudinal PID scale multiplies only the feedback (P+I) terms; the feedforward (kf) keeps its tuned value instead of being scaled along with it. The lateral PID scales have their own toggle.

items.title: Honda Nidec: ECU-matched longitudinal improvements
items.description: Honda Nidec only. Shapes the longitudinal command to match the factory ECU - rate-limits the acceleration command to the ECU's ramp rates, applies a speed-dependent coasting deadband (wide at low speed, tight on the highway), and briefly coasts through gas/brake transitions to avoid lurch. Calibrated on the 2019 Pilot; other Nidec cars may need tuning. OFF = stock command path.

items.title: Live Learning Gas
items.description: Allows Honda gas and wind compensation factors to learn live while driving.

items.title: Try Honda Bosch Radar (experimental)
items.description: EXPERIMENTAL â€” Honda Bosch radar. When ON, openpilot reads the factory Bosch radar's fine-range objects (0x280) and feeds them into the longitudinal controller.

items.title: Stopping Decel Rate
items.description: Brake-rate limiter used while coming to a stop (carcontroller).

items.title: Stop Accel
items.description: Target acceleration once stopped (holds the brake).

items.title: Planner Stopping Rate
items.description: How quickly commanded deceleration ramps down while coming to a stop.

items.title: vEgo Stopping
items.description: Speed (m/s) below which the planner treats the car as stopping.

items.title: vEgo Starting
items.description: Speed (m/s) above which the car is considered moving again.

items.title: Honda Dashboard Variant B
items.description: Honda clusters round the cruise set-speed (km/h to mph) two different ways. Variant A (3 dashed lane lines drawn, the default) and Variant B (4 dashed lane lines) round differently, so the same speed reads e.g. 60 on A vs 61 on B. Turn ON if your cluster is Variant B. Placeholder for now - has no effect until the rounding correction is built.

items.title: Interactivity Timeout
items.description: Apply a custom timeout for settings UI. This is the time after which settings UI closes automatically if user is not interacting with the screen.

sections.title: HUD Elements
sections.description: Overlays shown on the driving screen

items.title: Show Blind Spot Warnings
items.description: Enabling this will display warnings when a vehicle is detected in your blind spot as long as your car has BSM supported.

items.title: Steering Arc
items.description: Display steering arc on the driving screen when lateral control is enabled.

items.title: Display Turn Signals
items.description: When enabled, visual turn indicators are drawn on the HUD.

items.title: Display Road Name
items.description: Displays the name of the road the car is traveling on. The OpenStreetMap database of the location must be downloaded to fetch the road name.

items.title: Standstill Timer
items.description: Show a timer on the HUD when the car is at a standstill.

items.title: Real-time Acceleration Bar
items.description: Show an indicator on the left side of the screen to display real-time vehicle acceleration and deceleration. This displays what the car is currently doing, not what the planner is requesting.

sections.title: Developer UI Info
sections.description: Speedometer and debug display options

items.title: Developer UI
items.description: Display real-time parameters and metrics from various sources.

items.title: Speedometer: Always Display True Speed
items.description: For applicable vehicles, always display the true vehicle current speed from wheel speed sensors.

items.title: Speedometer: Hide from Onroad Screen
items.description: When enabled, the speedometer on the onroad screen is not displayed.

sections.title: Alerts & Extras
sections.description: Traffic light alerts and visual flair

items.title: Green Traffic Light Alert (Beta)
items.description: A chime and on-screen alert will play when the traffic light you are waiting for turns green and you have no vehicle in front of you. On-screen visual alert is only available on comma 3X. Note: This chime is only designed as a notification. It is the driver's responsibility to observe their environment and make decisions accordingly.

items.title: Lead Departure Alert (Beta)
items.description: A chime and on-screen alert will play when you are stopped, and the vehicle in front of you start moving. On-screen visual alert is only available on comma 3X. Note: This chime is only designed as a notification. It is the driver's responsibility to observe their environment and make decisions accordingly.

items.title: Tesla Rainbow Mode
items.description: Display a rainbow effect on the path the model wants to take. It does not affect driving in any way.

items.title: Enable sunnypilot
items.description: Use the sunnypilot system for adaptive cruise control and lane keep driver assistance. Your attention is required at all times to use this feature.

items.title: Enable Lane Departure Warnings
items.description: Receive alerts to steer back into the lane when your vehicle drifts over a detected lane line without a turn signal activated while driving over 31 mph (50 km/h).

items.title: Always-On Driver Monitoring
items.description: Enable driver monitoring even when sunnypilot is not engaged.

items.title: Use Metric System
items.description: Display speed in km/h instead of mph.

sections.title: Recording
sections.description: Camera and audio recording during drives

items.title: Record and Upload Driver Camera
items.description: Upload data from the driver facing camera and help improve the driver monitoring algorithm.

items.title: Record and Upload Microphone Audio
items.description: Record and store microphone audio while driving. The audio will be included in the dashcam video in comma connect.

sections.title: General
sections.description: Power, boot, and unit preferences

items.title: Wake Up Behavior
items.description: Controls state of the device after boot/sleep. Default: Device will boot/wake-up normally and will be ready to engage. Offroad: Device will be in Always Offroad mode after boot/wake-up.

items.title: Max Time Offroad
items.description: Device will automatically shutdown after set time once the engine is turned off. 30h is the default.

sections.title: Updates
sections.description: Control software updates

items.title: Disable Updates
items.description: When enabled, software updates will be off. This requires a reboot to take effect.

sections.title: nrdr Force Update
sections.description: Trigger a remote device update.

items.title: Force Update
items.description: Flip ON to run the full updater chain on the device (check, download, install, reboot). The device flips this back OFF when it picks up the request - that is your acknowledgment. Only works while the car is off. Watch Remote Action Status below for progress.

panels.label: Developer
panels.description: Debug tools, remote access, and advanced services

sections.title: Connectivity
sections.description: Remote access and debugging interfaces

items.title: Enable ADB
items.description: ADB (Android Debug Bridge) allows connecting to your device over USB or over the network. See https://docs.comma.ai/how-to/connect-to-comma for more info.

items.title: sunnypilot Longitudinal Control (Alpha)
items.description: WARNING: sunnypilot longitudinal control is in alpha for this car and will disable Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB). On this car, sunnypilot defaults to the car's built-in ACC instead of sunnypilot's longitudinal control. Enable this to switch to sunnypilot longitudinal control. Enabling Experimental mode is recommended when enabling sunnypilot longitudinal control alpha. Changing this setting will restart sunnypilot if the car is powered on.

sections.title: Test Maneuvers
sections.description: DANGER: enabling these maneuvers replaces normal driving behavior with deterministic test sequences. Each toggle requires explicit confirmation per write. Use only in a closed environment.

items.title: [TEST] Lateral Maneuver Mode
items.description: Replaces normal lateral control with a deterministic test sequence. NOT for road use.

items.title: [TEST] Longitudinal Maneuver Mode
items.description: Replaces normal longitudinal control with a deterministic test sequence. NOT for road use.

items.title: Show Advanced Controls
items.description: Toggle visibility of advanced sunnypilot controls. This only changes the visibility of the toggles; it does not change the actual enabled/disabled state.

items.title: GitHub Runner Service
items.description: Enables or disables the GitHub runner service.

items.title: copyparty Service
items.description: copyparty is a very capable file server, you can use it to download your routes, view your logs and even make some edits on some files from your browser. Requires you to connect to your comma locally via its IP address.

sections.title: Model Behavior

items.title: Use Lane Turn Desires
items.description: If you are driving at 20 mph (32 km/h) or below and have your blinker on, the car will plan a turn in that direction at the nearest drivable path. This prevents situations (like at red lights) where the car might plan the wrong turn direction.

items.title: Adjust Lane Turn Speed
items.description: Set the maximum speed for lane turn desires.

items.title: Live Learning Steer Delay
items.description: Allow device to learn and adapt car's steering response time

items.title: Adjust Software Delay
items.description: Adjust the software delay when Live Learning Steer Delay is toggled off. The default software delay value is 0.2

items.title: Neural Network Lateral Control (NNLC)
items.description: Use a neural network for lateral control instead of the default torque controller.

sections.title: Camera
sections.description: Camera position and calibration

items.title: Adjust Camera Offset
items.description: Virtually shift camera's perspective to move model's center to Left(+ values) or Right (- values)

items.title: Stop and Go for Manual Parking Brake (Beta)
Enforce Factory Longitudinal Control
items.description: sunnypilot will not take over control of gas and brakes. Factory Toyota longitudinal control will be used.

items.title: Stop and Go Hack (Alpha)
items.description: sunnypilot will allow some Toyota/Lexus cars to auto resume during stop and go traffic. This feature is only applicable to certain models that are able to use longitudinal control. This is an alpha feature. Use at your own risk.
